sections.overview: The common toad is a widespread Eurasian amphibian that spends much of the year on land and returns to water to breed.
sections.identification: It has dry-looking warty skin, relatively short hind legs and prominent glands behind the eyes.
sections.habitat: Outside the breeding season it uses woodland, scrub, gardens and other damp terrestrial refuges; breeding takes place in still or slow water.
sections.diet: Adults eat invertebrates such as slugs, snails and insects; the exact diet changes with prey availability.
sections.behavior: Seasonal movements bring adults back to breeding waters, and they often walk rather than make long leaps.
sections.reproduction: Females lay long gelatinous strings of eggs in water, where the tadpoles develop.
sections.ecology: As a land-foraging predator and aquatic breeder, it connects terrestrial feeding areas with freshwater habitats.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment classifies the species globally as Least Concern, while noting habitat-related threats and declines in some areas.
